approach: Fault: StateDir::clean_job (state.rs:113) discards the removal error and measures nothing. Change it to return a CleanReport {bytes, error: Option<(PathBuf, String)>}. Bytes are the whole job directory's allocated size (st_blocks*512, each (dev,ino) counted once, no symlink following), measured just before pin::remove_tree. Add one helper in state.rs, report_clean(ui, &CleanReport), that the five call sites use after the closing commit succeeds. It emits 'reclaimed 11.4 GB' via ui.line, or 'warning: could not remove <path>: <err>'. A missing or empty directory prints nothing. Call sites: manage.rs:135 and 224; run.rs:2276, 2451 (non-blocked only) and 2568. The Ui trait (lib.rs:101) has only line(); the CLI Terminal in main.rs:366 just prints it. So display.rs, pin.rs and athena.toml need no change.

decisions.choice: Keep per-job target directories; delete the job directory on close and report the bytes reclaimed. The shared-target question goes in decisions.md; athena.toml is unchanged.
decisions.reason: Review 2 R14 showed a shared target dir ran another job's stale test binaries. Per-job isolation (D46) is what the checks need. Deleting on close removes the disk growth.

rejected.why: Reuses stale test binaries (R14), contends for cargo's build lock, and is out of scope.

decisions.choice: Report the size of the whole job directory (it is what is deleted), described as 'reclaimed'. Tests compare it to an independent walk, not to the planted target/ size alone.
decisions.reason: The job directory also holds plan-N/read-N snapshots, job.lock, live/, usage/ and pr-link.json, so target/ alone would under-describe what is freed. The line reports actual freed space.

rejected.why: Adds a second measurement and a longer line; the operator cares about total space freed.
Fails because other files are in the directory, or is circular if it reuses the function under test.

decisions.choice: Measure allocated bytes: MetadataExt::blocks()*512, count each (dev, ino) once, use symlink_metadata and do not follow symlinks.
decisions.reason: Cargo hard-links artifacts (target/debug/<bin> and deps/<bin>-hash), and sparse files differ in apparent length. Allocated bytes count what is actually freed.

rejected.why: Double-counts hard links and overstates sparse files.

decisions.choice: clean_job returns a report and the caller prints one ui line; removal failure only warns and the close stays Ok.
decisions.reason: One place measures and formats, so every closing path reports the same way. The records are already committed, so failing the close would make the job look unclosed.

rejected.option: Fail the close on removal error
rejected.why: The commit is done; the job would look unclosed.

rejected.option: Add a reclaimed field to Closed/Finished structs
rejected.why: Wider change across consumers; a ui line meets the criterion.

decisions.choice: Write format_bytes in state.rs (decimal units, one decimal: B, KB, MB, GB, TB). Do not touch display.rs.
decisions.reason: No existing formatter exists. Ui::line is implemented by Terminal in main.rs, which only prints, so no CLI rendering change is needed.

rejected.why: It does not format ui.line output, so there is nothing to change there.

decisions.choice: Make removal fail in tests by putting a regular file at the job-directory path (remove_dir_all gives ENOTDIR, even for root). In the same test, first show that a normal directory at that path is removed cleanly.
decisions.reason: pin::remove_tree clears the immutable flag on the top directory and restores write bits, so mode bits and chattr +i on the top directory cannot block root. A file at the path always fails and needs no cleanup or chattr support.

rejected.why: Depends on filesystem support, needs teardown, and the test could skip.
Root bypasses them, so they prove nothing.

files.purpose: clean_job returns CleanReport; allocated-bytes walk with (dev,ino) dedup; format_bytes; report_clean helper; unit tests incl. hard-link pair counted once.
Use report_clean at lines 135 and 224, after the commit.
Tests per closing path, removal failure, kept-dir cases; update any exact-output assertions.
Record the shared target directory question, alternatives, R14 evidence and decision.
Entry for build cache deletion and space reclaimed.
One-line note that closing deletes the job's build cache and reports space reclaimed.

steps: Rewrite StateDir::clean_job in state.rs to return CleanReport (walk by symlink_metadata using blocks()*512 and a (dev,ino) set, then pin::remove_tree, capturing the error with the path). Add format_bytes and report_clean(&dyn Ui, &CleanReport). Unit-test the walk with a hard-linked pair and nested files, the dir removal, the error path, and format_bytes.
Replace the five call sites in manage.rs and run.rs with clean_job plus report_clean, each still after its closing commit, keeping the Blocked exception at run.rs:2451.

Add lifecycle.rs tests: one per closing path (landed, failed, rejected, abandoned, interrupted then close, closed while blocked) with an independent pre-close walk and a 'reclaimed ' line check. Add the removal-failure test (file at the job-dir path, with a control showing a normal dir is removed), the no-warning-when-empty test, and the kept-dir tests (blocked, failed commit). Fix any exact-output tests.
Write the decisions.md entry (next free number), the CHANGELOG entry and the README note. Do not touch athena.toml, display.rs or pin.rs.
Run cargo fmt --all, cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings and cargo test --locked.

risks.risk: The block-count walk differs across filesystems (for example on overlay or tmpfs), so exact-equality tests could flake.
risks.mitigation: Tests compare against an independent walk that uses the same blocks()*512 and (dev,ino) rules. They plant files of at least a block.

risks.risk: Existing tests that assert exact closing output break because of the new line.
risks.mitigation: Emit the line only when bytes > 0 or there is an error, and update the affected assertions.

risks.risk: A removal failure leaves a 12 GB directory.
risks.mitigation: The warning names the path so the operator can delete it; the close still succeeds because the commit is done.

risks.risk: A walk of a 12 GB tree is slow.
risks.mitigation: It is metadata only, one pass, before removal.

demonstrations.method: Unit test in state.rs: plant a job dir with target/ files plus other files (job.lock, live/x), call clean_job, assert the dir is gone and report.bytes equals an independent test-local walk (st_blocks*512) taken just before the call and is at least the planted target/ allocation. Lifecycle tests in lifecycle.rs: close each path (landed, failed, rejected, abandoned, interrupted then `athena close`, closed while blocked). On the go paths the fake producer or a test hook writes a multi-block target/ file during dispatch, before the closing commit. On the close paths the test plants target/ in the job dir first. Each test records the independent walk of the job dir just before the closing step, then asserts the dir is absent and the 'reclaimed ' line shows format_bytes of that number.
demonstrations.observes: Every closing path leaves no job directory, and the reported byte count equals the independent measurement and is at least the planted size.
demonstrations.fails_without: If any path skipped cleanup, the dir would remain. If clean_job did not measure, no 'reclaimed' line would appear and the count would be 0.

demonstrations.method: Two checks. (1) A format_bytes unit test: 11_400_000_000 renders '11.4 GB', plus MB, KB and B cases. (2) Lifecycle tests capture the common/mod.rs Lines ui output of both `go` and `close`, and assert a line contains 'reclaimed ' followed by the formatted measured size. A job whose directory is absent or empty emits no line containing 'warning' and no failure.
demonstrations.observes: The closing output contains 'reclaimed <N> <unit>'. The nothing-to-remove job reports no failure.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the helper the line is missing and the contains assertion fails. A spurious warning on an empty dir would fail the no-warning assertion.

demonstrations.method: Lifecycle test (running as root): first set up a normal job dir at the path and show clean_job removes it with no error. Then put a regular file at the job-dir path and close. Assert a ui line begins with 'warning' and contains the job directory path, and that the close returns Ok. A unit test in state.rs checks that report.error carries the path.
demonstrations.observes: A warning line naming the path appears and the close still succeeds.
demonstrations.fails_without: With errors swallowed (`let _ =`), no warning is emitted and the assertion fails.

demonstrations.method: Tests: a job left Blocked after go still has its job dir and no 'reclaimed' line. A close whose commit is forced to fail (gate violation or an unwritable record) returns an error and leaves the dir intact. Interrupted-job inspection before `athena close` shows the dir present.
demonstrations.observes: The directory exists in each case and no reclaimed line was emitted.
demonstrations.fails_without: If cleanup ran before the commit or regardless of its result, the dir would be gone after the failed commit or while blocked.

demonstrations.method: Inspect the diff: a new decisions.md entry on the shared target directory, with alternatives, evidence citing docs/design/reviews/athena-v0-review-2.md R14, and the decision not to share. athena.toml has no diff.
demonstrations.observes: The entry is present with the evidence and the decision; athena.toml is unchanged.

demonstrations.command: cargo fmt --all --check && cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings && cargo test --locked
demonstrations.fails_without: Unformatted code, lints or failing tests would make a command exit nonzero.

demonstrations.method: Inspect the diff for a CHANGELOG entry under the unreleased heading saying that closing a job deletes its build cache and reports the space reclaimed, plus the README note.
demonstrations.observes: The entry and the README line are present.

open_questions: How the go-path tests plant a target/ file mid-run (fake producer writing into the job's CARGO_TARGET_DIR versus a test hook before the closing commit) depends on the harness in tests/common; the producer must read it.
Whether a go-path run can reach a state where the interrupted job's dir is locked by a live process at close; close_with checks the registry, assumed safe.
